Create a native pixel-art SPRITE SHEET CORRECTION for Cloud Strife from original Final Fantasy VII (1997), matching the attached original Cloud game reference: golden spiky hair, sleeveless purple SOLDIER clothing, brown boots, gloves, one steel shoulder guard, enormous broad steel BUSTER SWORD with clipped point and red-brown hilt. No Remake redesign or alternate weapon. Transparent RGBA background. Landscape 2:1 canvas, ideally 1024x512. EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS and TWO ROWS: EIGHT complete full-body sprites, no text, no labels, no grid lines, no floor, no platform or scenery. Detailed crisp pixel art consistent with the reference. Face right. Every body, boot, hand, blade tip must be fully contained in its cell with clear transparent margins. Four sequential poses in every row must differ in anatomy, elbow bend, torso angle, leg posture and sword orientation. Never duplicate or merely translate a pose.
This is BRAVER, Cloud's FFVII first Limit Break: a leap and a powerful VERTICAL DOWNWARD SWORD CLEAVE. It is not Cross-slash, not Omnislash. NO X slash, no crossed trails, no horizontal beam, no magical rune, no giant blue arc, no separate effect fragments. Frame2: vertical descending cut, arms drive the sword downward in front of torso, steel blade nearly vertical with tip pointing below hands, one knee opening as Cloud descends. Frame3: ground-level impact posture on an invisible floor, deeply bent front knee, torso leaned forward, both hands grip the vertical sword whose point is at sole level, back leg extends for balance; do not paint any floor or dust cloud. Frame4: recovery, torso rises and bends less, rear foot steps inward, blade is pulled diagonally upward from the low impact to a guard in front of chest. These are four different real physical poses.
ROW 2: chargeRelease, a heavier BRAVER release adapted to the project's charge mechanic. Frame1: compressed airborne release after push-off, knees tucked asymmetrically, torso straighter, sword fully overhead held by both hands. Frame2: forceful downward chopping phase, torso and elbows drive forward/down with blade point under the right shoulder and legs spread back; full-body genuinely airborne silhouette. Frame3: deep heavy landing with both knees bent, shoulders folded down and the heavy sword held point-down just ahead of front boot, readable low braced impact. Frame4: heavy-cut recovery, one foot braces far back, front knee still bent, both hands draw the sword up alongside torso and head lifts. Give row2 distinct anatomy from row1, not copies. Keep both rows equally spaced, subjects complete with margins. No effects crossing cells. This is generated adapted animation, not a claim of official source-game frames.
